query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: Non-metallic inclusions in Q235 steel create localized galvanic cells that trigger pitting corrosion, and reducing inclusion content through refining suppresses degradation.
generation.material_initial_state: Pre-exposure Q235 steel in its standard condition, containing typical non-metallic inclusions and impurities.
generation.intervention: Utilize metallurgical refining or controlled melting practices to produce a batch of Q235 steel with a significantly reduced inclusion content while retaining an equivalent batch in the standard state.
generation.conditions: Subject both the purified and conventional steel samples to identical exposure in a chloride-bearing solution (3.5 wt.% NaCl) at both room temperature and elevated temperatures.
generation.structural_mediator: Localized micro-galvanic sites formed at the interfaces between the steel matrix and non-metallic inclusions (e.g., MnS or oxides).
generation.mechanism: Electrochemical potential differences at the steel–inclusion interfaces form galvanic cells in the presence of an electrolyte, accelerating pitting and localized corrosion. Reducing the inclusion content minimizes these galvanic sites, thereby lowering corrosion initiation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Purified Q235 steel samples will exhibit lower pitting density, shallower pits, and reduced overall corrosion rates compared to standard samples when exposed to harsh corrosive environments.
generation.baseline: Untreated, standard Q235 steel with typical inclusion concentrations exhibiting known pitting corrosion behavior.
generation.boundary: This mechanism applies in chloride-rich media where galvanic interactions are significant; variations in inclusion composition and distribution may modulate the effect.
generation.uncertainty: Although the role of inclusions in galvanic corrosion is documented in similar steels, the degree of improvement from inclusion reduction may vary due to processing and inclusion variability.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of Q235 steel samples—one with conventional inclusion content and another processed for reduced inclusions using refining methods. Expose both sets under identical experimental conditions in a standardized chloride solution at controlled room and elevated temperatures, then compare corrosion morphology and rates.
measurements: Characterization of inclusion content (SEM with EDS)
Pitting density and pit depth measurements via microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the purified samples do not display a statistically significant reduction in pitting corrosion and overall corrosion rate compared to the standard samples, the hypothesis that inclusions are the primary drivers of localized galvanic corrosion would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: (1) The (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating was prepared by plasma spraying on substrate of the Q235 steel, consisting of a simple FCC solid solution with Laves phase, and the coating bonded well to the substrate. (2) Elemental segregation occurred between the dendrites and the interdendrites of the coating, and the elements Cr and Nb with high melting point were enriched between the interdendrites. This phenomenon may be due to the difference in melting point of the element and the characteristics of the plasma spraying process. (3) The coating has a microhardness of 321 HV0.5, which can effectively improve the surface hardness of the Q235 steel part. (4) The (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating exhibited excellent corrosion resistance in the electrochemical corrosion test of a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution comparing to previously studied coatings prepared by other processes. (5) In the 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, the selective corrosion occurred on the surface of (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating, while the interdendritic phase rich in Nb and Cr was preferentially corroded as an anode, and the dendritic phase rich in Co, Ni, and Fe was protected as a cathode.
